title: Kwomtari language - Wikipedia
text: Kwomtari is the eponymous language of the Kwomtari family of Papua New Guinea. Spencer (2008) is a short grammar of Kwomtari. The language has an SOV [clarification needed] constituent order and nominative–accusative alignment. Both subjects and objects are marked suffixally on the verb.

title: Kwomtari–Fas languages - Wikipedia
text: The Kwomtari–Fas languages, often referred to ambiguously as Kwomtari, are an apparently spurious language family proposal of six languages spoken by some 4,000 people in the north of Papua New Guinea, near the border with Indonesia.

title: Senu River languages - Wikipedia
text: January 15, 2025 - The Senu River languages are a small language family spoken in the Senu River watershed of Papua New Guinea. They consist at least of the Kwomtari languages, Kwomtari and Nai, with several additional languages more distantly related to them.
